title: Optimizing LZSM protocol for high-fidelity gates in open-system fluxonium
authors: Santiago Ferreyra, Valentın Reparaz, Maria Jose Sanchez, Leandro Tosi, Daniel Dominguez
abstract: Quantum gates based on resonant Rabi oscillations are inherently slow for small-frequency qubits. They are also prone to errors due to counter-rotating terms. However, when the anharmonicity is sufficiently high, as in the fluxonium architecture, alternative manipulation protocols can outperform standard resonant driving. In this work, we implement fast, high-fidelity quantum gates based on a one-period Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana (LZSM) driving protocol. We derive analytical expressions that simplify the exploration of the parameter space while accounting for the multi-level structure of the circuit. Furthermore, we analyze the role of leakage, discussing strategies to mitigate it and identifying regimes in which it becomes the dominant source of error. Finally, to evaluate the impact of dissipation on gate fidelity, we develop a robust formalism suitable for analyzing the open-system performance of quantum gates in the strong driving regime.
summary: The paper develops and optimizes fast quantum gates for fluxonium qubits using the Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana (LZSM) protocol. It rigorously models open system dynamics by incorporating multi-level effects and dissipation via a Floquet-Born-Markov master equation. The key finding is that minimizing gate error requires careful tuning of driving parameters to suppress leakage, leading to high-fidelity gates in the strong driving regime.
main_problem: The primary goal is optimizing fast, high-fidelity quantum gates for low-frequency qubits while overcoming limitations imposed by standard resonant driving and accounting for multi-level structure and dissipation.
main_result: LZSM protocols provide a superior method for achieving fast gate operations in fluxonium circuits. The fidelity optimization shows that leakage errors dominate the error budget, suggesting mitigation through specific driving frequency choices.
method: The authors employ advanced theoretical techniques including Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana (LZSM) driving protocols, Floquet theory, and deriving time-dependent master equations to model open-system dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting fluxonium circuit. The analysis moves from the full Hamiltonian to effective two-level systems using techniques like bare truncation and the Floquet-Schrieffer-Wolf (FSW) Hamiltonian, culminating in a Floquet-Born-Markov master equation for open dynamics.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($ ar{F}$), transition probability ($P_{01}$), leakage rate ($L$), and total gate time ($t_g$).
important_parameters: Driving parameters include drive frequency ($\omega_d$) and amplitude ($A$); system parameters involve superconducting energies ($E_J, E_C, L_L$). The strong driving regime is of particular interest.
main_assumptions: Approximations include the Floquet-Born-Markov (FBM) master equation framework and using a 'moderated rotating-wave approximation' to simplify the time-dependent Liouvillian super-operator.

paper_structure: The paper builds from analyzing the basic LZSM protocol in an idealized two-level system to incorporating multi-level structure via FSW Hamiltonians, and finally developing a robust formalism using the Floquet-Born-Markov master equation to quantify open-system performance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the practical limitations of superconducting qubits by providing rigorous theoretical tools (FBM master equation) to analyze gate errors beyond simple RWA, which is crucial for scaling quantum processors.
